title: Kenyan Coconut Mandazi
author: Chef Amina Hassan

relatedDish.note: KEN102 (Coconut Mandazi) is an enhanced version of KEN015 (Authentic Kenyan Mandazi), with extra coconut milk and grated coconut for a richer, more intensely coconut-flavoured result. KEN015 is the classic everyday mandazi; KEN102 is the indulgent coastal version.

desc: Coconut Mandazi — the most indulgent version of Kenya's beloved fried bread. Extra coconut milk and fresh grated coconut in the dough create a richer, more intensely fragrant result than classic mandazi. Pure coastal morning bliss.
longDesc: Coconut mandazi doubles down on what makes mandazi great — the coconut. Where the classic version uses coconut milk as the liquid, this version also incorporates freshly grated coconut or desiccated coconut into the dough, intensifying the flavour dramatically. The result is a mandazi that is slightly moister, more fragrant, and more distinctly coastal in character.
ingredients: ½ cup freshly grated coconut or desiccated coconut
steps: Combine flour, sugar, baking powder, cardamom, and salt.
Mix coconut milk, warm water, grated coconut, egg, and melted butter together.
Combine wet and dry ingredients into a soft dough.
Roll to 1cm thick. Cut into triangles or squares.
Deep fry at 170°C for 2—3 minutes per side until golden.
chefTips: Fresh grated coconut gives a far superior flavour to desiccated — worth the effort.
Rest the dough the full hour for best texture.
Medium oil temperature — too hot burns the outside before the inside cooks.
commonMistakes: Oil too hot — browned outside, raw inside.
storage: Airtight container for 3 days. Freeze for 2 months.
reheating: Warm in oven at 160°C for 5 minutes.
culturalNote: Coconut mandazi is the coastal elevation of the everyday mandazi — the version prepared for special mornings, celebrations, and whenever the full Swahili coconut flavour is called for.
